notice: RN bank batch 129: Mental health case studies: serotonin syndrome, MAOI hypertensive crisis, anorexia and bulimia. Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026. See REVIEW-LOG.md. Also carries the bank-wide catalog (catalog.py): the RN Question Bank and every curated test set.

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that suggest serotonin syndrome.

rationale.correct: Clonus with agitation, fever and diarrhea after adding serotonergic drugs is serotonin syndrome.
references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: For each drug, indicate whether it adds to serotonin syndrome risk with fluoxetine.

columns.text: Does not add to the risk

rationale.correct: Many non-psychiatric drugs add serotonin.
references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The first step is {{b1}}; if symptoms persist, the provider may give {{b2}}.

options.text: stopping all serotonergic drugs and giving supportive care
giving more tramadol for the shaking
cyproheptadine and a benzodiazepine for agitation

rationale.correct: Stop the drugs, support and give cyproheptadine if needed.
references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Which interventions should the nurse anticipate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Acetaminophen as the main cooling method

rationale.correct: Benzodiazepines, fluids, monitoring and cooling.

perOption.e: Fever is from muscle activity, not the brain's set point.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

exhibits.title: Orders
exhibits.body: Stop fluoxetine, tramadol, dextromethorphan. Lorazepam IV. Cyproheptadine if needed.

questions.stem: Which actions should the nurse take to prevent a repeat event? Select all that apply.

options.text: Add the interaction to the medication record
Teach the client to check with a pharmacist before any OTC cough or cold remedy
Report the dental prescription interaction to the prescriber
Tell the client to restart fluoxetine tomorrow with tramadol at half dose

rationale.correct: Document the interaction, teach and inform prescribers.

perOption.e: This is an interaction, not an allergy.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Take action to prevent drug interactions.

questions.stem: At 24 hours, for each finding or statement, indicate whether it shows improvement or understanding, or needs follow-up.

rows.text: "I'll use acetaminophen for my tooth pain."
"I'll start St John's wort to replace the fluoxetine."
Low mood returning with poor sleep

rationale.correct: Recovered; depression needs a planned restart.

perOption.r5:c1: Depression needs a plan; fluoxetine has a long half-life before any new drug.
perOption.r5:c2: Depression needs a plan; fluoxetine has a long half-life before any new drug.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that suggest a hypertensive crisis from the MAOI.

rationale.correct: A tyramine meal on an MAOI caused a hypertensive crisis.
references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize cues of MAOI hypertensive crisis.

questions.stem: For each food, indicate whether it is high in tyramine or safe in usual amounts.

rationale.correct: Aged, fermented and cured foods are high in tyramine.
references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The client is at greatest risk for {{b1}}, so the goal is to {{b2}}.

options.text: lower the blood pressure promptly but in a controlled way
bring it to normal within minutes

rationale.correct: Controlled lowering prevents stroke.

perOption.b2:b: Can cause stroke from low perfusion.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

questions.stem: Which interventions should the nurse anticipate? Select all that apply.

options.text: IV phentolamine or another short-acting agent as prescribed
Nifedipine capsule punctured under the tongue

rationale.correct: Short-acting IV agents with monitoring.

perOption.f: A sympathomimetic that worsens the crisis.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: The psychiatrist plans to switch the client from phenelzine to sertraline. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Keep the tyramine diet for 2 more weeks
Start sertraline the day after phenelzine stops to avoid a relapse
Give meperidine for the headache while the MAOI is still active

rationale.correct: A 14-day washout and continued diet are needed.
references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: At discharge, for each statement, indicate whether it shows understanding or needs more teaching.

rows.text: "For 2 weeks I'll still avoid aged cheese, cured meat and tap beer."
"I won't take decongestants or cough medicines without asking."
"A severe headache means I should go to the emergency department."
"Fresh fruit and fresh meat are fine."

rationale.correct: Diet, interactions and washout timing.
references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that indicate the client needs hospital admission.

rationale.correct: Bradycardia, orthostasis, hypothermia, long QTc and very low BMI need admission.

perOption.r6: A sign of starvation but not an admission criterion.

references: Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize cues of medical instability in anorexia.

questions.stem: For each finding, indicate whether it fits anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa or both.

rows.text: Normal weight with binge and purge cycles
Intense fear of weight gain and body image distortion

rationale.correct: Weight separates the two; body image and electrolytes are shared.
references: Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: During the first week of feeding, the most dangerous complication is {{b1}}, shown by {{b2}}.

options.text: falling phosphorus with heart failure or dysrhythmias

rationale.correct: Refeeding syndrome is the first-week danger.

perOption.b1:a: Shifts of phosphate, potassium and magnesium.

references: Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Which parts of the admission plan should the nurse include? Select all that apply.

options.text: Daily phosphorus, potassium and magnesium for the first week
Weigh at the same time in a gown after voiding, back to the scale
Observe the client for 1 hour after meals
Allow the client to choose to skip meals if anxious
Let the client exercise to burn off anxiety

rationale.correct: Electrolytes, careful weighing, supervision and monitoring.
references: Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

exhibits.title: Admission
exhibits.body: Nutrition starts at 1,600 kcal/day and increases. Thiamine and phosphate supplements.

questions.stem: At lunch, the client says, "If I eat this, I'll be huge. You just want me to get fat." Which responses are therapeutic? Select all that apply.

options.text: "This meal is part of your treatment. I'll sit with you while you eat."
"It sounds like eating feels very frightening right now."
"Your body needs this food to keep your heart working."
"You look skeletal; you need to eat."
"If you don't finish, you'll lose your phone privileges for a week."

rationale.correct: Firm support, empathy and a health focus.
references: Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

exhibits.title: Day 3
exhibits.body: Client cut food into tiny pieces and hid some in a napkin at breakfast.

questions.stem: On day 5, for each finding, indicate whether it shows improvement or needs follow-up.

rationale.correct: Progress, but low phosphorus and edema signal refeeding syndrome.
references: Laboratory reference ranges as used in common NCLEX review texts; follow the facility's ranges
Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that require immediate action.

rationale.correct: Severe hypokalemia with ectopy is the emergency.

perOption.r3: Metabolic alkalosis from vomiting worsens hypokalemia.
perOption.r4: Needs dental care, but not urgent.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: For each finding, indicate its cause.

rows.text: Chronic diarrhea and dependence for bowel movements

rationale.correct: Vomiting causes alkalosis and dental damage; both cause potassium loss.
references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

options.text: IV and oral potassium replacement on a cardiac monitor
a laxative to clear the bowel
no faster than about 10 mEq/hr through a peripheral line
only after the client agrees to stop vomiting

rationale.correct: Replace potassium safely on a monitor.
references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Potassium chloride 20 mEq in 100 mL is to be infused over 2 hours through a peripheral line. At what rate should the nurse set the pump? Record your answer in mL/hr.

rationale.correct: 100 mL / 2 hours = 50 mL/hr, which gives 10 mEq/hr.
references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

exhibits.title: Orders
exhibits.body: KCl 20 mEq in 100 mL over 2 hours x3. Oral KCl 40 mEq. Magnesium level.

questions.stem: The client is admitted to an eating disorder unit. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Supervise the bathroom for 1 to 2 hours after meals
Agree on a regular meal schedule with the client
Explore feelings that come before a binge
Allow laxatives to continue to avoid constipation
Weigh the client several times a day to show progress

rationale.correct: Supervision, regular meals, trigger work and laxative tapering.
references: Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Take action in the eating disorder unit.

questions.stem: At 4 weeks, for each statement or finding, indicate whether it shows progress or needs follow-up.

rows.text: Purging down from six times a day to once a week
"When I feel lonely at night, I call a friend instead of bingeing."
"I brush my teeth right after I vomit."
"I'm still using a few laxatives at night."

rationale.correct: Fewer purges and new coping; ongoing laxatives and dental care need attention.

perOption.r4:c1: Rinse with water first; brushing straight after spreads acid.
perOption.r4:c2: Rinse with water first; brushing straight after spreads acid.

references: Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)

caseStudies.title: Serotonin syndrome from fluoxetine with tramadol

exhibits.title: Emergency department
exhibits.body: A 46-year-old client takes fluoxetine 40 mg daily for depression. After a dental extraction 2 days ago, the client was prescribed tramadol and also took an over-the-counter cough syrup with dextromethorphan. Since this morning the client has been restless, sweating and shaking.

exhibits.title: Emergency department
exhibits.body: A 58-year-old client with treatment-resistant depression takes phenelzine. Two hours after a wine-tasting dinner with aged cheeses and cured salami, the client has a pounding headache in the back of the head, a stiff neck and palpitations.

exhibits.title: Primary care
exhibits.body: A 17-year-old client is brought by a parent because of weight loss over 8 months. The client runs 10 km a day, eats "only salad" and says, "I'm still too fat around my stomach." The client has not had a period for 5 months and fainted at school yesterday.

rows.label: Skin
cells: Fine hair on the arms and back

exhibits.title: Emergency department
exhibits.body: A 24-year-old client of normal weight comes in with palpitations and muscle cramps. The client admits to binge eating then vomiting up to six times a day and taking 20 laxative tablets a day for a year.

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
testSets.description: Works like the real NCLEX-RN: each question depends on your answers so far, and the exam stops once your result is clear, after 85 to 150 questions. Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
